overall_summary: Analysis of FACTVERSE performance reveals that space-related 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary anomalies (particularly those involving extreme environments, liquid diamonds, and unusual time/physics concepts) achieve the highest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view) among recent 7-day uploads. Standard quick facts and animal trivia show lower immediate velocity compared to immersive hypothetical space scenarios.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) outperform standard space facts within the first week.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' planetary immersion concepts with extreme physical stakes.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring extreme planetary conditions such as 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (968 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views) drive high view counts.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more deep-space anomalies highlighting bizarre physics defying everyday human intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) show very low velocity and engagement.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize psychological trick shorts unless tied to a high-stakes narrative or mystery micro-story.
